title: Picou's upturned-bell clarinet
summary: Joe says Picou's clarinet was made with an upturned bell, like a saxello, and Joe was the only one he let touch it.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Did Picou have that clarinet with the funny upturned bell? All the time he had that.
I really don't know. From what I understand, he got it from some old Frenchman
Was it just a regular clarinet with a bell that went under it...?
Or was it a regular clarinet that was made with that upturned bell?
It was made with that bell on it.
I mean, Dizzy uses that upturned trumpet, he claims, because he can hear himself play. Did Picou ever say anything like that, or did he just...
No. I was the only that could ever touch that clarinet, I'll tell you that. They put out another thing a lot similar to that thing called a saxello.
I've never even heard of that.
To a clarinet. And this thing for me, I don't know, I think it was really a saxello. But anyway, it had that little turned-up bell.
It was pitched at B-flat or what?

Yes, it was a B-flat. It was a clarinet. But it got a distinctly different tone. You noticed. But we would be on sessions a lot of times in Los Angeles... And Picou had a daughter who lived here, you know, for a long time. And we'd have a lot of musicians that wanted to... He
said, "You can't touch that. Joe's the only one that can touch it."
